description: Caravelle number 249, first flown 2 April 1968, delivered to Sterling, later the personal aircraft of Emperor Bokassa, then Europe Aero Service and Air Toulouse; displayed at the entrance to the association's field. Wears Air Toulouse colours.
Breguet 765 Sahara, the transport version of the Deux-Ponts; a unique survivor in the collection.
Number 3, one of the last two of the type; formerly displayed at Ambérieu air base, then used as a dynamic cinema in an Ardèche theme park before being bought back and returned to Toulouse.
Coded AY, delivered to the French Air Force on 2 June 1965, first served with EB 1/93 in Guyane and later with every Mirage IV bomber squadron; converted to Mirage IVP in 1985.
One of 74 Mirage 2000N; served with EC 2/4 La Fayette and allocated to the association by the French Air Force in 2019; carries the La Fayette badge on the left fin.
Wears a special scheme for the 50th anniversary of escadron de chasse 3/3 Ardennes; withdrawn 7 June 1994 and brought by road from Châteauroux in 2005.
Painted in the Djibouti Vixen colours. The association holds two Mirage IIIC (86 and 90); which is inside Aeroscopia and which on the association field needs checking on site.
Converted from an F1C-200; coded 30-QY and flown by the Normandie-Niémen regiment of the 30e escadre until 2008; dismantled at Châteaudun by an association team.

Came from the Château de Savigny-lès-Beaune collection wearing the number 251 and Patrouille de France colours, which it never carried in service; the real serial is 215. Previously displayed at the Abbeville-Drucat aero club as 215 / 2-EN.

Mystère IV A number 44, arrived from Cazaux in 1983 nominally via the US Air Force Museum; repainted as Captain Larrayadieu's Patrouille de France aircraft. A second Mystère IV, number 1, is stored dismantled.
Mystère IV number 1, held dismantled in the association's store.
aliases: Mystère IVA; Mystere IV; MD452 n1

description: Brought by road from Rochefort air base in 1985.

Pre-production airframe number 06, later brought to production standard and flown by escadrille 59S; recovered at Rochefort by Ailes Anciennes Armorique, displayed at Vannes-Monterblanc, and inherited by Ailes Anciennes Toulouse in May 2014.
Served with flottilles 14F and 11F and took part in the 1983 Baalbek raid; ended its career with the deck-crew school at Hyères, recovered June 2018.
aliases: SEM; Super Etendard; Super Etendard M

description: Number 397, first flown February 1980 as a Falcon 20F and seen in the film Le Professionnel; converted in 1984 to Falcon 200 engines and hydraulics.
Flown in from Avord air base in 1983.
E5, part of the French production head series; first flew 30 November 1978 and was delivered to the CEAM at Mont-de-Marsan for type evaluation.
Stored at the Toulouse flight test centre and blown over in the January 2009 storm, losing canopy, nose and fin; rescued from scrapping in July 2009 and rebuilt with recovered parts.
Restored by the association in Patrouille de France colours; obtained in exchange for Magister 103, which went to the IUT de Rangueil.
Flown in from Tours air base in 1984 and repainted in Hawaii Air National Guard colours.
aliases: T33A; T-33A; T-Bird; Shooting Star; T33

description: Flew with the 11e escadre, was returned to the Americans and joined the Bitburg base collection; obtained in 1995 when that base closed. Remains the property of the National Museum of the USAF.
Served with the Minnesota Air National Guard; arrived from Davis-Monthan in December 1990 on loan from the National Museum of the USAF, shipped free of charge by the French Navy.
Ex-Hellenic Air Force Thunderstreak. Two serials (52-6789 and 53-6760) appear on the association's page and it is not clear which belongs to this airframe, so the serial is left blank.
A composite airframe: the rear fuselage came from Bourges in 1982 and the wings from the Cazaux range.
Flown in from the Brétigny flight test centre in 1984.
Ex-Swiss Air Force; flown in from Payerne in August 1995.
Came from an English technical school in 1988.
Ex-East German MiG-21, later carried the Luftwaffe number 22+86.
Flown in from the Cazaux flight test centre in 1981.
Fuselage only. Ended up on the Suippes range in the Marne, recovered in 1971 by Ailes Anciennes Alsace and passed to Toulouse in 1987; the only Espadon preserved.
Bare-metal Noratlas of the association's collection.
Brought by road from Montauban in 1982.
Target drone recovered dismantled from Biscarrosse in 1998, fully restored and mounted on a trailer for travelling displays.
Research delta aircraft recovered in 1984; after several restoration attempts in schools it returned to the collection and moved into the new hangar in 2015.
Arrived from Graulhet in 1984.
Brought by road from Montauban in 1982 with the wings removed.
Brought by road from Réalmont in 1982, a gift from Maurice Bosc.
Built September 1965 as an MS.881 with a Potez 4E20; converted to MS.880B with a Continental O-200A in 1987 and grounded after an engine failure on 13 October 2007.
Light touring aircraft of the collection.
Air Force basic trainer in the association's collection.
Belonged to the Toulouse flight test centre, which gave it to the association in September 2009.
Former Centre d'essais en vol aircraft, made available by the DGA in September 2009; displayed near the shop and regularly opened to visitors.
Recovered from the ENAC in April 2017 where it was a teaching airframe, hence the cutaways in the wings, fuselage and engine.
L-4J Cub; arrived from Meaux in 1986.
aliases: J3C; J-3C; L-4J; Cub; J3; L4J

description: Came from Escatalens in 1987; stored dismantled awaiting display space.
Came from Escatalens in 1986.
Light amateur design in the collection.
Druine D.31 Turbulent serial 168, built by Léo Chagnes and granted its CNRA on 25 July 1957; won a special Ministry of Air prize in 1957.
Practically finished but never flown; recovered from a loft in the Paris region in 1993.
Came from Saint-Dié in 1987.
Came from Escatalens in 1986.
Microlight in the collection.
Given by a private owner in March 2007 together with the Bijave; both had been stored in a barn near Toulouse. Kept under cover in the storage hangar.
Given by a private owner in March 2007 together with the Squale, from a barn near Toulouse.
Two-seat training glider; arrived from Niort in 1992.
Wooden training glider in the collection.
Glider number 9, previously F-CBXS; given by M. Jouhaud in 1985.
Glider serial 200; came from Itxassou in 1985.
Glider number 118; arrived from Balma in 1991.
Transferred from the Musée de l'Air in 1996; stored under cover awaiting hangar space before restoration.
Built by de Havilland Canada at Downsview in 1958 as a CS2F-2 for the Royal Canadian Navy and used as the CS2F-3 prototype; later a Sécurité Civile water bomber.
aliases: S2FT; S-2FT; Turbo Firecat; Tracker; S2

description: Number 5, in service with the French Navy from 6 July 1959 to 13 April 1977 and never modernised; flew with flottilles 2S, 4F and 6F and was displayed at BAN Nîmes before transfer. Recorded as undergoing full restoration in the February 2025 ARDHAN naval inventory.
Arrived from Cognac air base in 1987; an early restoration has weathered and a second is planned.
Sikorsky H-19 of the association's helicopter collection.
The Flying Banana; arrived in 1989 on deposit from the Musée de l'ALAT at Dax. Serial from the ARDHAN inventory of preserved French naval aircraft dated February 2025.
aliases: H21C; H-21C; Banane; Flying Banana; H21

description: First Djinn, arrived from Montauban in 1993 and restored by the association's helicopter team.
Used for years as a spares source at Perpignan; given to the association in 2005 and awaiting completion and restoration.
The yellow Alouette II, arrived from Marcoussis in 2008; a composite of several versions used as a spares source for the Navy Alouette II now in Aeroscopia. Restoration began in 2012.
The first production twin-engine Écureuil; first flew 11 March 1980, stayed with the manufacturer for trials and later went to a regional technical school before joining the collection in 1995.
VE 111 C experimental vehicle bought in the early 1990s from a Toulouse school; degraded by storage and three moves, awaiting restoration before display.
Served with the Royal Air Force and was deployed to Pakistan; postwar sold for survey work in the Caribbean, then abandoned in a corner of Toulouse-Blagnac airport where the association recovered it.
aliases: C47A; C-47A; DC-3; Dakota; C47; DC3
